headline: Daily research brief — Wednesday, October 21

items.detail: Tesla Q3 2026 (provisional: secondary sources only, two source sets conflict materially and the primary release could not be read — ir.tesla.com returned 403 and the earnings 8-K was not yet on EDGAR at 16:33 ET). On Set A, revenue was $28.05B, roughly flat year on year and a slight miss against Tesla's own $28.34B consensus, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.45 consensus. GAAP operating income of $718M fell about 56% year on year, but auto gross margin ex-credits improved quarter on quarter (16.3% to 18.1%), so the profit decline is opex-driven, not margin-driven. The pre-event straddle priced a ±5.56% move against a 7.77% eight-quarter average — the market underpriced the magnitude, and the avoid-premium-into-the-binary rule was the correct posture. The stock was up about 1.9% shortly after the release (Barron's). MSFT and AAPL are the remaining in-window binaries.
items.title: TSLA reported AMC today; the binary is over and the avoid-premium call was right

items.detail: The WTI curve is in steep backwardation (Dec26 $97.80 to Dec27 $81.43, −$16.37 or −16.7% over 12 months) and distillate stocks sit 9% below the five-year average after today's on-schedule EIA print: crude drew 3.06M bbl (third straight draw) while distillates built 1.7M bbl against a −1.3M expected draw. At least 18 vessel attacks in two weeks, with Iran now targeting tankers beyond Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman, is the live binary; mediation prospects are deemed distant. Grains are pricing abundance instead: harvest is rolling (soy 64% complete, corn 44%) and fronts are in carry, even as China buys US beans aggressively. Caveat: the rates desk failed today (FRED unreachable), so the discount-rate leg of the growth-multiple read is blind — do not infer a rates regime from this package.
items.title: Prompt energy tightness is the macro read of the day

items.detail: NVDA's front-week implied volatility fell from 36.19% to 30.48% on healthy quotes (65k/11k volume, strikes near spot), the largest single-day move across the watchlist. It still sits about 6 points above the trailing 20-day realized 24.23% on a clean window (0.237, not window-contingent), so this is not complacency. The read is event-calendar drift — nothing sits in the front week with NVDA's earnings not until Nov 18 — not mispricing. SPY is the mild version: 10.83% front IV against 9.18% realized on a clean window, about 1.6 points of normal front-week carry. QQQ (19.03% vs 15.86% realized) stays window-contingent (0.341) — no clean verdict.
items.title: NVDA front-week IV collapsed 570 bps — the largest single-day repricing on the board

items.detail: MSFT's Oct-30 IV of 36.2% against a 24.27% near-weekly is the textbook earnings hump with the Oct 28 print inside the window — expected term shape, not richness. Short gamma into Oct 28 stays on the avoid list (consensus: EPS $4.71–$4.73, revenue $90.65B). AAPL's Nov-6 straddle implies ±5.00% on a 15.2-day window against a 2.46% single-day historical average — window-inflated, not directly comparable — with six of the last eight prints down-but-small. Selling into Nov 2 is short gamma into a binary: avoid. All earnings dates verified against today's Nasdaq calendar sweep.
items.title: MSFT's Oct 28 earnings are priced correctly in term shape; AAPL's Nov 2 binary is window-inflated
